Although the form itself is about precision, the texture is all about rhythm. I’m not worried about symmetry here, I’m chasing feeling. That raw, tactile surface that invites you to turn the piece over in your hands. There’s gonna be a lot of pretty great monsters in the batch. I feel like I’m honing in on my glazing techniques and my construction is getting better and better. Sometimes I wonder if I’m stagnating because I’m working with in certain parameters, but also I feel like in terms of craftsmanship I’m growing. I’m really starting to realize how much you gain by repeatedly doing the same motions and repeatedly using the same general concepts… making these monsters has been such a great Zen like practice. I’ve never really appreciated or understood production pottery or how you could make the same bowl or the same mug, and while this isn’t really that I am using some of the same building techniques the basic thing stays the same, and then it’s really just variables that create these characters, and I’m kind of enjoying the practice of it. #vermontartist #ceramics #scarymonster #kilnreveal
